text:
nik: Quick follow-up to the dedicated GPU pool autoscale RFC. I want to finalize the boundary between SLA-weighted admission and general burst admission. Proposal: introduce a thin policy evaluator that enforces per-tenant SLA-bands and delegates actual capacity changes to the existing autoscaler.

maria: thin evaluator = admission gate + accounting only? we should avoid adding a second active scaler. :+1:

sam: agree. keep it stateless where possible. can we model SLA band as a per-tenant token-bucket so runtime stays simple?

lee: token-bucket is okay but we need a clear degrade path. once SLA tokens drain, do we reject, fallback to cheaper model variants, or both? different tenants will want different behavior.

nik: design sketch: SLA band gives prioritized tokens. When exhausted we take two possible actions (tenant-configurable): 1) soft admission rejection with structured retry guidance 2) auto-fallback to a configured ordered list of cheaper/quantized model variants. Example policy snippet (for human readability only):

```
# tenant policy (not executable here)
sla_weight: 0.7
token_bucket_capacity: 1200
token_refill_per_min: 400
fallbacks:
  - gptx-s-8q
  - gptx-2b-int8
```

maria: that looks clean. one improvement: make refill adaptive to observed p95 latency so the bucket auto-adjusts to avoid starving or overshooting.

sam: adaptive refill is useful but watch oscillation. use EWMA smoothing over a minute and a min refill floor.

lee: ops needs observability: an "sla_band_depleted" event and metric tags (tenant_id, action) so SREs can alert. otherwise we won't know who is being throttled.

infra-bot: deploy update: autoscaler-proxy v0.9 canaryed in cluster-b, no rollbacks.

nik: ops signal + metrics is planned. open question: where does the policy evaluator live? options we considered: (A) admission webhook in operator, (B) central control-plane proxy, (C) runtime-side admission inside the runtime process.

maria: tradeoffs: webhook easy for mutation but adds request-path latency; control-plane proxy centralizes reasoning and eventing but needs HA; runtime-side is lowest latency but policy changes are heavier to ship.

sam: leaning to control-plane proxy. we can rollout with dry-run, and it simplifies audit logs and metrics emission.

lee: testing idea: build a simulation harness that replays recent traffic traces and runs the policy evaluator offline to estimate P95 impact and cost delta per tenant. simple batch job that outputs CSVs.

nik: yes. sim job should compute: admission_rejections, fallback_invocations, tokens_consumed, estimated_cost_delta. use a day's traces for representative signals.

maria: implementation note: policy evaluator should be pure and side-effect free so dry-run equals live decisions. record decisions separately and emit events only when enforcement is enabled.

sam: rollout plan (draft): 1) implement pure policy evaluator + dry-run sim, 2) ship control-plane proxy in canary with dry-run for 7d, 3) enable enforcement for up to 5 tenants, 4) expand tenants and add fallback variants after validating metrics.

lee: another tradeoff to decide: rejection vs rate-limit with Retry-After. Many clients will aggressively retry on 429 and worsen pressure. we should return a structured error that suggests backoff and links to tenant console to opt into fallback. also include a short human-friendly message.

nik: agreed. include Retry-After and X-Redwood-Fallback-URL headers in 429 responses when applicable. also surface per-tenant burn-rate and forecast in Console.

maria: who owns the sim harness? I can take the first pass this week and push a data-driven CSV report.

sam: I'll prototype the control-plane proxy API and a YAML schema for policies.

lee: I'll add metrics shape and error payload spec to the telemetry docs and mock dashboards.

nik: logging: keep a single audit stream of policy decisions (ndjson) and publish to Kafka topic `sla-policy-decisions.v1`. infra already approved the topic.

infra-bot: notice: topic `sla-policy-decisions.v1` created; retention=14d.

nik: follow-ups: maria -> sim PR, sam -> proxy sketch PR, lee -> metrics + error format PR. post PR links here when ready. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
